حالِهِمْ. وقِيلَ: إنَّما بَنَوْا ذَلِكَ البُنْيانَ لِئَلّا يَغْشى السَّيْلُ أمْوالَهم فَيُهْلِكَها، فَكانُوا يَفْتَحُونَ مِن أبْوابِ السَّدِّ ما يُرِيدُونَ، فَيَأْخُذُونَ مِنَ الماءِ ما يَحْتاجُونَ إلَيْهِ، وكانَتْ لَهم جَنَّتانِ عَنْ يَمِينِ وادِيهِمْ وعَنْ شِمالِهِ، فَأخْصَبَتْ أرْضُهُمْ، وكَثُرَتْ فَواكِهُهُمْ، وإنْ كانَتِ المَرْأةُ لَتَمُرُّ بَيْنَ الجَنَّتَيْنِ والمِكْتَلُ عَلى رَأْسِها، فَتَرْجِعُ وقَدِ امْتَلَأ مِنَ الثَّمَرِ ولا تَمَسُّ بِيَدِها شَيْئًا مِنهُ، ولَمْ يَكُنْ [يُرى] في بَلَدِهِمْ حَيَّةٌ ولا عَقْرَبٌ ولا بَعُوضَةٌ ولا ذُبابٌ ولا بُرْغُوثٌ، ويَمُرُّ الغَرِيبُ بِبَلْدَتِهِمْ وفي ثِيابِهِ القَمْلُ، فَيَمُوتُ القَمْلُ لِطِيبِ هَوائِها. وقِيلَ لَهُمْ: ﴿كُلُوا مِن رِزْقِ رَبِّكم واشْكُرُوا لَهُ بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾ أيْ: هَذِهِ بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ، أوْ بَلْدَتُكم بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ، ولَمْ تَكُنْ سَبِخَةً ولا فِيها ما يُؤْذِي ﴿وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ أيْ: واللَّهُ رَبٌّ غَفُورٌ، وكانَتْ ثَلاثَ عَشْرَةَ قَرْيَةً، فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ إلَيْهِمْ ثَلاثَةَ عَشَرَ نَبِيًّا، فَكَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ، ولَمْ يُقِرُّوا بِنِعَمِ اللَّهِ، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَأعْرَضُوا﴾ أيْ: عَنِ الحَقِّ، وكَذَّبُوا أنْبِياءَهم ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ العَرِمِ﴾ وفِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ أقْوالٍ.

(p. 445) أحَدُها: أنَّ العَرِمَ: الشَّدِيدُ، رَواهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أبِي طالِبٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. وقالَ ابْنُ الأعْرابِيِّ: العَرِمُ: السَّيْلُ الَّذِي لا يُطاقُ.

والثّانِي: [أنَّهُ] اسْمُ الوادِي، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ قَتادَةُ، والضَّحّاكُ، ومُقاتِلٌ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ المُسَنّاةُ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ، وأبُو مَيْسَرَةَ، والفَرّاءُ، وابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ. وقالَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: العَرِمُ: جَمْعُ عِرَمَةٍ، وهِيَ: السِّكْرُ والمُسَنّاةُ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ العَرِمَ: الجُرَذُ الَّذِي نَقَبَ عَلَيْهِمُ السِّكْرَ، حَكاهُ الزَّجّاجُ.

وَفِي صِفَةِ إرْسالِ هَذا السَّيْلِ عَلَيْهِمْ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى بَعَثَ عَلى سِكْرِهِمْ دابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ فَنَقَبَتْ فِيهِ نَقْبًا، فَسالَ ذَلِكَ الماءُ إلى مَوْضِعٍ غَيْرِ المَوْضِعِ الَّذِي كانُوا يَنْتَفِعُونَ بِهِ، رَواهُ العَوْفِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. وقالَ قَتادَةُ والضَّحّاكُ في آخَرِينَ: بَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ جُرَذًا يُسَمّى الخُلْدَ- والخُلْدُ: الفَأْرُ الأعْمى- فَنَقَبَهُ مِن أسْفَلِهِ، فَأغْرَقَ اللَّهُ [بِهِ] جَنّاتِهِمْ، وخَرَّبَ بِهِ أرْضَهم.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ أرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ ماءً أحْمَرَ، أرْسَلَهُ في السَّدِّ فَنَسَفَهُ وهَدَمَهُ وحَفَرَ الوادِيَ، ولَمْ يَكُنِ الماءُ أحْمَرَ مِنَ السَّدِّ، وإنَّما كانَ سَيْلًا أُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ﴾ يَعْنِي اللَّتَيْنِ تُطْعِمانِ الفَواكِهَ ﴿جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَواتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ﴾ قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، ونافِعٌ، وعاصِمٌ، وابْنُ عامِرٍ، وحَمْزَةُ، والكِسائِيُّ: " أُكُلٍ " بِالتَّنْوِينِ. وقَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو: " أُكُلِ " بِالإضافَةِ. وخَفَّفَ الكافَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ ونافِعٌ، وثَقَّلَها الباقُونَ. أمّا الأُكُلُ، فَهو الثَّمَرُ.

وَفِي المُرادِ بِـ الخَمْطِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ. (p. 446) أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الأراكُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، والجُمْهُورُ؛ فَعَلى هَذا، أُكُلُهُ: ثَمَرُهُ؛ ويُسَمّى ثَمَرُ الأراكِ: البَرِيرَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ كُلُّ شَجَرَةٍ ذاتِ شَوْكٍ، قالَهُ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ كُلُّ نَبْتٍ قَدْ أخَذَ طَعْمًا مِنَ المَرارَةِ حَتّى لا يُمْكِنَ أكْلُهُ، قالَهُ المُبَرِّدُ والزَّجّاجُ. فَعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ، الخَمْطُ: اسْمٌ لِلْمَأْكُولِ، فَيَحْسُنُ عَلى هَذا قِراءَةُ مَن نَوَّنَ الأُكُلَ؛ وعَلى ما قَبْلَهُ، هو اسْمُ شَجَرَةٍ، والأُكُلُ ثَمَرُها، فَيَحْسُنُ قِراءَةُ مَن أضافَ.

فَأمّا الأثْلُ، فَفِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الطَّرْفاءُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ. والثّانِي: أنَّهُ السَّمُرَ، حَكاهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ شَجَرٌ يُشْبِهُ الطُّرَفاءَ إلّا أنَّهُ أعْظَمُ مِنهُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَشَيْءٍ مِن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾ فِيهِ تَقْدِيمٌ، وتَقْدِيرُهُ: وشَيْءٌ قَلِيلٌ مِن سِدْرٍ، وهو شَجَرُ النَّبْقِ. والمَعْنى أنَّهُ كانَ الخَمْطُ والأثْلُ في جَنَّتَيْهِمْ (p. 447) أكْثَرَ مِنَ السِّدْرِ. قالَ قَتادَةُ: بَيْنا شَجَرُهم مِن خَيْرِ الشَّجَرِ، إذْ صَيَّرَهُ اللَّهُ مِن شَرِّ الشَّجَرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ﴾ أيْ: ذَلِكَ التَّبْدِيلَ جَزَيْناهم ﴿بِما كَفَرُوا وهَلْ نُجازِي إلا الكَفُورَ﴾.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: قَدْ يُجازى المُؤْمِنُ والكافِرُ، فَما مَعْنى هَذا التَّخْصِيصِ؟ فَعَنْهُ جَوابانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ يُجْزى ولا يُجازى، فَيُقالُ في أفْصَحِ اللُّغَةِ: جَزى اللَّهُ المُؤْمِنَ، ولا يُقالُ: جازاهُ، لِأنَّ " جازاهُ " بِمَعْنى كافَأهُ، فالكافِرُ يُجازى بِسَيِّئَتِهِ مِثْلَها، مُكافَأةً لَهُ، والمُؤْمِنُ يُزادُ في الثَّوابِ ويُتَفَضَّلُ عَلَيْهِ، هَذا قَوْلُ الفَرّاءُ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ الكافِرَ لَيْسَتْ لَهُ حَسَنَةٌ تُكَفِّرُ ذُنُوبَهُ، فَهو يُجازى بِجَمِيعِ الذُّنُوبِ، والمُؤْمِنُ قَدْ أحْبَطَتْ حَسَناتُهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ، هَذا قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ. وقالَ طاوُوسٌ: الكافِرُ يُجازى ولا يُغْفَرُ لَهُ، والمُؤْمِنُ لا يُناقَشُ الحِسابَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ هَذا مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لِسَبَإٍ﴾؛ والمَعْنى: كانَ مِن قِصَصِهِمْ أنّا جَعَلْنا بَيْنَهم ﴿وَبَيْنَ القُرى الَّتِي (p. 448) بارَكْنا فِيها﴾ وهِيَ: قُرى الشّامِ؛ وقَدْ سَبَقَ بَيانُ مَعْنى البَرَكَةِ فِيها [الأنْبِياءِ: ٧١] هَذا قَوْلُ الجُمْهُورِ. وحَكى ابْنُ السّائِبِ أنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى لَمّا أهْلَكَ جَنَّتَيْهِمْ قالُوا لِلرُّسُلِ: قَدْ عَرَفْنا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنا، فَلَئِنْ رَدَّ إلَيْنا ما كُنّا عَلَيْهِ لَنَعْبُدَنَّهُ عِبادَةً شَدِيدَةً، فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِمُ النِّعْمَةَ، وجَعَلَ لَهم قُرًى ظاهِرَةً فَعادُوا إلى الفَسادِ وقالُوا: باعِدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا، فَمُزِّقُوا.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قُرًى ظاهِرَةً﴾ أيْ: مُتَواصِلَةٌ يَنْظُرُ بَعْضُها إلى بَعْضٍ ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا فِيها السَّيْرَ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم كانُوا يَغْدُونَ فَيَقِيلُونَ في قَرْيَةٍ، ويَرُوحُونَ فَيَبِيتُونَ في قَرْيَةٍ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ، وقَتادَةُ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ جَعَلَ ما بَيْنَ القَرْيَةِ والقَرْيَةِ مِقْدارًا واحِدًا، قالَهُ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سِيرُوا فِيها﴾ والمَعْنى: وقُلْنا لَهُمْ: سِيرُوا فِيها ﴿لَيالِيَ وأيّامًا﴾ أيْ: لَيْلًا ونَهارًا ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ مِن مَخاوِفِ السَّفَرِ مِن جُوعٍ أوْ عَطَشٍ أوْ سَبُعٍ أوْ تَعَبٍ. وكانُوا يَسِيرُونَ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ في أمانٍ، فَبَطَرُوا النِّعْمَةَ ومَلُّوها كَما مَلَّ بَنُو إسْرائِيلَ المَنَّ والسَّلْوى فَقالُوا رَبَّنا بَعِّدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ، وأبُو عَمْرٍو: " بَعِّدْ " بِتَشْدِيدِ العَيْنِ وكَسْرِها. وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، وعاصِمٌ، وحَمْزَةُ: " باعِدْ " بِألِفٍ وكَسْرِ العَيْنِ. وعَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ كالقِراءَتَيْنِ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: إنَّهم قالُوا: لَوْ كانَتْ جَنّاتُنا أبْعَدَ مِمّا هِيَ، كانَ أجْدَرَ أنْ يُشْتَهى جَناها. قالَ أبُو سُلَيْمانَ الدِّمَشْقِيُّ: لَمّا ذَكَّرَتْهُمُ الرُّسُلُ نِعَمَ اللَّهِ، أنْكَرُوا أنْ يَكُونَ ما هم فِيهِ نِعْمَةً، (p. 449) وَسَألُوا اللَّهَ أنْ يُباعِدَ بَيْنَ أسْفارِهِمْ. وقَرَأ يَعْقُوبُ: [ " رَبُّنا " بِرَفْعِ الباءِ] " باعَدَ " بِفَتْحِ العَيْنِ والدّالِ، جَعَلَهُ فِعْلًا ماضِيًا عَلى طَرِيقِ الإخْبارِ لِلنّاسِ بِما أنْزَلَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وجَلَّ بِهِمْ. وقَرَأ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أبِي طالِبٍ، وأبُو عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ [السُّلَمِيُّ]، وأبُو رَجاءٍ، وابْنُ السَّمَيْفَعِ، وابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: " بَعُدَ " بِرَفْعِ العَيْنِ وتَخْفِيفِها وفَتْحِ الدّالِ مِن غَيْرِ ألِفٍ، عَلى طَرِيقِ الشِّكايَةِ إلى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ. وقَرَأ عاصِمٌ الجَحْدَرِيُّ، وأبُو عِمْرانَ الجَوْنِيُّ: " بُوعِدَ " بِرَفْعِ الباءِ وبِواوٍ ساكِنَةٍ مَعَ كَسْرِ العَيْنِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَظَلَمُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: بِالكُفْرِ وتَكْذِيبِ الرُّسُلِ. والثّانِي: بِقَوْلِهِمْ " بَعِّدْ بَيْنَ أسْفارِنا ".

﴿فَجَعَلْناهم أحادِيثَ﴾ لِمَن بَعْدَهم يَتَحَدَّثُونَ بِما فُعِلَ بِهِمْ ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهم كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ أيْ: فَرَّقْناهم في كُلِّ وجْهٍ مِنَ البِلادِ كُلَّ التَّفْرِيقِ، لِأنَّ اللَّهَ لَمّا غَرَّقَ مَكانَهم وأذْهَبَ جَنَّتَيْهِمْ تَبَدَّدُوا في البِلادِ، فَصارَتِ العَرَبُ تَتَمَثَّلُ في الفِرْقَةِ بِسَبَأٍ ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ﴾ أيْ: فِيما فُعِلَ بِهِمْ ﴿لآياتٍ﴾ أيْ: لَعِبَرًا ﴿لِكُلِّ صَبّارٍ﴾ عَنْ مَعاصِي اللَّهِ ﴿شَكُورٍ﴾ لِنِعَمِهِ،

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾ " عَلَيْهِمْ " بِمَعْنى " فِيهِمْ "، (p. 450) وَصِدْقُهُ في ظَنِّهِ أنَّهُ ظَنَّ بِهِمْ أنَّهم يَتَّبِعُونَهُ إذْ أغْواهُمْ، فَوَجَدَهم كَذَلِكَ. وإنَّما قالَ: ﴿وَلأُضِلَّنَّهم ولأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾ [النِّساءِ: ١١٩] بِالظَّنِّ، لا بِالعِلْمِ، فَمَن قَرَأ: " صَدَّقَ " بِتَشْدِيدِ الدّالِ، فالمَعْنى: حَقَّقَ ما ظَنَّهُ فِيهِمْ بِما فُعِلَ بِهِمْ؛ ومَن قَرَأ بِالتَّخْفِيفِ، فالمَعْنى: صَدَقَ عَلَيْهِمْ في ظَنِّهِ بِهِمْ.

وَفِي المُشارِ إلَيْهِمْ قَوْلانِ.

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهم أهْلُ سَبَإٍ. والثّانِي: سائِرُ المُطِيعِينَ لِإبْلِيسَ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَما كانَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن سُلْطانٍ﴾ قَدْ شَرَحْناهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ﴾ [الحِجْرِ: ٤٢]. قالَ الحَسَنُ: واللَّهِ ما ضَرَبَهم بِعَصًا ولا قَهْرَهم عَلى شَيْءٍ إلّا أنَّهُ دَعاهم إلى الأمانِيِّ والغُرُورِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إلا لِنَعْلَمَ﴾ أيْ: ما كانَ تَسْلِيطُنا إيّاهُ إلّا لِنَعْلَمَ المُؤْمِنِينَ مِنَ الشّاكِّينَ. وقَرَأ الزُّهْرِيُّ: " إلّا لِيُعْلَمَ " بِياءٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ عَلى ما لَمْ يُسَمَّ فاعِلُهُ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ يَعْمَرَ: " لِيَعْلَمَ " بِفَتْحِ الياءِ.

وَفِي المُرادِ بِعِلْمِهِ هاهُنا ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ، قَدْ شَرَحْناهُ في أوَّلِ (العَنْكَبُوتِ: ٣).

﴿وَرَبُّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ مِنَ الشَّكِّ والإيمانِ ﴿حَفِيظٌ﴾. وقالَ ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ: والحَفِيظُ بِمَعْنى الحافِظِ. قالَ الخَطّابِيُّ: وهو فَعِيلٌ بِمَعْنى فاعِلٍ، كالقَدِيرِ، والعَلِيمِ، فَهو يَحْفَظُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ بِما فِيها لِتَبْقى مُدَّةَ بَقائِها، ويَحْفَظَ عِبادَهُ مِنَ (p. 451) المَهالِكِ، ويَحْفَظَ عَلَيْهِمْ أعْمالَهُمْ، ويَعْلَمَ نِيّاتِهِمْ، ويَحْفَظَ أوْلِياءَهُ عَنْ مُواقَعَةِ الذُّنُوبِ، ويَحْرُسُهم مِن مَكايِدِ الشَّيْطانِ.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 34, verses 22–23:**

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed (to be gods) besides Him﴾. The meaning is: Say to the disbelievers, "Call upon those whom you claimed to be gods, that they may bestow a favour upon you or remove an affliction from you." Then He informed about them, saying: ﴿They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾, meaning of good or evil, benefit or harm. ﴿And they have no share in them (the heavens and the earth)﴾, meaning they did not share with Us in anything of their creation. ﴿And He has not from them any supporter﴾, meaning that He has none of the gods as a helper in anything.

﴿And intercession with Him will not benefit except for one whom He permits﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read *adhina lahu* (أَذِنَ لَهُ) with a fatha on the alif. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read *udhina lahu* (أُذِنَ لَهُ) with a damma on the alif. And from 'Asim there are two readings like these. (These are the *qira'at*, the canonical modes of recitation.) The meaning is: the intercession of no angel or prophet will benefit unless permission is granted to him to intercede. It has been said: until he is permitted to intercede for whomever he intercedes. In this there is a refutation of them when they said, "Indeed these gods intercede for us."

﴿Until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾. Most readers recite *fuzzi'a* (فُزِّعَ) with a damma on the fa' and a kasra on the zay. Ibn Qutaybah said: the terror has been lightened from them. al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that the terror has been lifted from their hearts. Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub and Aban read *faza'a* (فَزَعَ) with a fatha on the fa' and the zay, and the verb is attributed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Ya'mar read *faragha* (فَرَغَ) with an unpointed ra' and a pointed ghayn. It has the same meaning as the first, because the hearts have emptied of terror. Others said: rather, they have been emptied of doubt and polytheism.

Concerning those referred to there are two opinions.

The first: they are the angels. The speech indicates that they are terrified by a matter that befalls them from the command of Allah, though it is not mentioned in the verse, because the removal of terror indicates that it has occurred. Concerning the cause of their terror there are two opinions.

The first: they are terrified by hearing the speech of Allah the Exalted. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah speaks by revelation, the people of the heavens hear a sound like the dragging of a chain over rock, so they fall in a swoon, and they remain so until Gabriel comes to them. When Gabriel comes to them, terror is removed from their hearts, and they say, 'O Gabriel, what has your Lord said?' He says, 'The truth.' Then they call out, 'The truth, the truth!'" Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels strike their wings in submission to His word, like the sound of a chain on smooth rock. When terror is removed from their hearts, they say, 'What has your Lord said?' They say, 'To the One who said the truth,' ﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾."

The second: they are terrified of the Hour rising. Concerning the reason they thought the Hour had drawn near so that they were terrified, there are two opinions.

The first: when there was the interval (*fatrah*) between 'Isa and Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, and then Allah sent Muhammad, Allah sent down Gabriel with the revelation. When he descended, the angels thought that he had come with something of the matter of the Hour, so they fell in a swoon because of that. Gabriel began passing by every heaven, removing terror from them and informing them that it was the revelation. This was said by Qatadah, Muqatil and Ibn al-Sa'ib. It has also been said: when they learned of the revelation to Muhammad (ﷺ), they were terrified, because they knew that his appearance was among the signs of the Hour.

The second: the angels who follow one another (*al-mu'aqqibat*), who visit the people of the earth and record their deeds, when Allah the Exalted sends them down, a loud sound is heard from them. Those angels below them think it is a matter of the Hour, so they fall prostrate and swoon until they know that it is not a matter of the Hour. This happens each time they pass by them. This was narrated by al-Dahhak from Ibn Mas'ud.

The second opinion: those referred to are the polytheists. Then there are two opinions concerning the meaning of the speech.

The first: the meaning is: until terror is removed from the hearts of the polytheists at death, as an establishment of proof against them, the angels say to them, "What did your Lord say in the world?" They say, "The truth." So they acknowledge it at a time when acknowledgment no longer benefits them. This was said by al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd.

The second: until the veil is removed from their hearts on the Day of Resurrection, it is said to them, "What has your Lord said?" This was said by Mujahid.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 34, verses 24–27:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ meaning the rain, and ﴿the earth﴾ meaning the vegetation and the fruit. He was only commanded to ask the disbelievers about this as an argument against them, that the One who provides is the One deserving of worship, and they do not affirm any provider other than Him. For this reason it was said to him: ﴿Say: Allah.﴾ Because they do not answer with anything other than this. And here the speech is complete. Then He commanded him to say to them: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ The position of the exegetes (tafsir, interpretation of the Qur'an) is that "aw" (or) here means "wa" (and). Abu Ubayda said: the meaning of the speech is, "Indeed we are upon guidance, and indeed you are in clear error." Al-Farra' said: the meaning of "aw" according to the exegetes is the meaning of "wa," and it is so in meaning, but Arabic does not use it that way. "Aw" does not stand in the place of "wa"; rather it is used in a matter left to choice, as you say: "If you wish, take a dirham or two," so he may take one or two, but he may not take three. The meaning of the verse is: "Indeed we are either astray or guided, and indeed you too are either astray or guided," while He knows that His Messenger is the guided one and that the other is the one who is astray. This is like when you say to a man whom you are denying, "By Allah, indeed one of us is a liar," and you mean him, so you have denied him in a way that is not explicit. Or a man says, "By Allah, so-and-so has arrived," and someone who knows his lie says to him, "Say: if Allah wills," thereby denying him in a manner better than an explicit denial. Among the speech of the Arabs is that they say "qatalahu Allah" (may Allah kill him), then they find it ugly, so they say "qata'ahu Allah," and some of them say "kata'ahu Allah." They say "ju'an" as an invocation against a man, then they find it ugly and say "judan," and some of them say "jusan." From this is their saying "waykaka" and "waysaka," and they mean the same as "waylaka" (woe to you), except that it is less severe than it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed in sin﴾ meaning, you will not be held accountable for it, ﴿and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ of disbelief and denial. The meaning is the declaration of disassociation from them. According to most of the exegetes, this verse has been abrogated (naskh, abrogation) by the Verse of the Sword, but there is no basis for that.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together﴾ meaning at the Resurrection in the Hereafter, ﴿then He will judge between us﴾ meaning He will decide ﴿with truth﴾ meaning with justice, ﴿and He is the Judge, the Knowing﴾ of what He decides. ﴿Say﴾ to the disbelievers, ﴿Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners﴾ meaning, inform me by what means you have attached them, when they do not create and do not provide. ﴿No!﴾ This is a rebuke and a warning. The meaning is: Turn back from this saying and be alerted from your error, for the matter is not as you are upon.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 34, verses 28–30:

(p-456) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾, meaning: general for all of creation. In the statement there is an inversion (taqdim), its implied sense being: "And We have not sent you except to mankind comprehensively." It was also said: the meaning of ﴿comprehensively to mankind﴾ is that you restrain them (takuffuhum) from the disbelief they are upon, and the ha' in it (kaffatan, i.e., the feminine ending) is for emphasis (mubalaghah).

﴿And they say: when is this promise?﴾ They mean the punishment with which he threatens them on the Day of Resurrection. They only said this because they deny the resurrection. ﴿Say: for you is the appointment of a Day﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions. The first: that it is the Day of Death at the time of the extraction (al-nazc) and the death-throes (al-siyaq), as reported by al-Dahhak. The second: it is the Day of Resurrection, as reported by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 34 (Saba'), verses 31–33:**

(p-٤٥٧) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved say: "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in that which came before it."﴾ He means the polytheists of Makkah, who say "We will never believe in the Qur'an, nor in that which is before it," meaning the Tawrah (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel). This was because the believers among the People of the Book said: "The description of Muhammad is in our Book," so the people of Makkah disbelieved in their Book.

Then He informed of their state on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾, meaning the polytheists of Makkah, in the Hereafter, ﴿returning the statement among themselves﴾, that is, some of them respond to others in argument and blame, ﴿those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant﴾, and they are the followers, saying to the leaders and chiefs: ﴿Had it not been for you, we would have been believers﴾, meaning, affirming the Oneness of God. The meaning is: you prevented us from faith. So the ones who were followed answered them, and said: ﴿Did we avert you from guidance after it came to you?﴾, meaning, did we prevent you from faith after the Messenger came to you? ﴿Rather, you were criminals﴾ by abandoning faith. In this there is a warning to the disbelievers that obedience of some of them to others in this world will become a cause of enmity in the Hereafter. Then the followers replied to them, saying: ﴿Rather, it was the plotting of the night and the day﴾, that is, rather, your plotting against us by night and by day.

Al-Farra' said: (p-٤٥٨) This is one of the things in which the Arabs use expansive speech because its meaning is clear, as they say: "Its night is standing (qa'im), and its day is fasting (sa'im)," so they attribute the action to things other than humans, while the meaning is for them. Al-Akhfash said: This is like His saying: ﴿from your town which has expelled you﴾ [Muhammad: 13]. Jarir said:

Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for "alladhi" (the feminine form "allati") to refer to both wealth and children together, since "amwal" (wealth) is a plural and "awlad" (children) is a plural. If you wish, you may take "allati" as referring to wealth and dispense with mention of children. He cited the verse of Mirar al-Asadi:

We have explained this in His saying: ﴿nor do they spend it in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Tawba: 34]. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: "Your wealth is not that which brings you near, nor are your children those who bring you near," and it was elided for brevity. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan and Abu al-Jawza' read: "bi-al-lati tuqarribukum" (with "allati"). Al-Akhfash said: ﴿Zulfa﴾ here is an ism al-masdar (a verbal noun used in place of the infinitive), as if he said: "It brings you near to Us in nearness." Ibn Qutayba said: ﴿Zulfa﴾ means nearness and station with Us.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿except one who believes﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: wealth does not bring near except to one who believes and uses it in obedience to Allah. ﴿Those will have the reward of double﴾, and what is meant by it here is ten good deeds. Its interpretation is: "They will have the double reward whose amount I have already informed you of."

Ibn Qutayba said: It has not come, as far as people of reflection see, and Allah knows best, that they will be rewarded with one like it, nor with two. Rather, He intended the reward of multiplication, which is a like added to a like of what it reaches. Hamza read: "fi al-ghurfa" (in the chamber), in the singular, intending the generic noun. **Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 34, verses 34–39:**

﴿And We did not send a warner to any town but its affluent ones said﴾, that is, a prophet who warns. They are its wealthy and its leaders.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "We have more wealth and children"﴾. Regarding those referred to, there are two views. The first is that they are the affluent of every nation. The second is that they are the polytheists of Makkah, who in their ignorance supposed that Allah had granted them wealth and children because of their honour before Him, so they said: ﴿And we are not going to be punished﴾, because Allah has been good to us by what He has given us, so He will not punish us. So He informed them that He ﴿extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾. The meaning is that the extension and restriction of provision are a trial and a test, not that extension indicates Allah's pleasure or that restriction indicates His displeasure. ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ this. Then He stated this meaning explicitly in His saying: ﴿Nor is your wealth or your children that which will bring you near to Us in position.﴾

Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for "alladhi" (the feminine form "allati") to refer to both wealth and children together, since "amwal" (wealth) is a plural and "awlad" (children) is a plural. If you wish, you may take "allati" as referring to wealth and dispense with mention of children. He cited the verse of Mirar al-Asadi:

We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, and opinions differ.

We have explained this in His saying: ﴿nor do they spend it in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Tawba: 34]. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: "Your wealth is not that which brings you near, nor are your children those who bring you near," and it was elided for brevity. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan and Abu al-Jawza' read: "bi-al-lati tuqarribukum" (with "allati"). Al-Akhfash said: ﴿Zulfa﴾ here is an ism al-masdar (a verbal noun used in place of the infinitive), as if he said: "It brings you near to Us in nearness." Ibn Qutayba said: ﴿Zulfa﴾ means nearness and station with Us.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿except one who believes﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: wealth does not bring near except to one who believes and uses it in obedience to Allah. ﴿Those will have the reward of double﴾, and what is meant by it here is ten good deeds. Its interpretation is: "They will have the double reward whose amount I have already informed you of."

Ibn Qutayba said: It has not come, as far as people of reflection see, and Allah knows best, that they will be rewarded with one like it, nor with two. Rather, He intended the reward of multiplication, which is a like added to a like of what it reaches. It is as though "al-di'f" (the double) means increase, so the meaning is: "They will have the reward of increase."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Mutawakkil, Ruways, and Zayd from Ya'qub read: ﴿lahum jaza'an﴾ with the accusative and tanwin, with the tanwin being kasra when connected, and ﴿al-di'fu﴾ in the nominative. Abu al-Jawza', Qatada and Abu 'Imran al-Jawni read: ﴿lahum jaza'un﴾ with the nominative and tanwin, and ﴿al-di'fu﴾ in the nominative.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-Mutawakkil read: "fi al-ghurfat" with a damma on the ghayn, a sukun on the ra', and an alif. Abu al-Jawza' and Ibn Ya'mar read: with a damma on the ghayn, a fatha on the ra', and an alif. ﴿Secure﴾ from death and from other things.

Muqatil said: meaning the angels and those who worshipped them. ﴿Then He will say to the angels, "Did these [people] used to worship you?"﴾ This is a question of confirmation and rebuke directed at the worshippers. The angels then glorified their Lord above association, so ﴿they will say, "Exalted are You"﴾, meaning: glorification of You from what they attributed to You of partners. ﴿You are our Protector, not them﴾, meaning: we disavow ourselves to You from them. Then Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So today﴾, meaning in the Hereafter, ﴿none of you will have power to benefit or harm one another﴾, meaning the worshippers and the worshipped, ﴿benefit﴾ through intercession, ﴿nor harm﴾ through punishment. ﴿And We will say to those who wronged﴾, that is, those who worshipped other than Allah, ﴿"Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny"﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Then He informed that they denied Muhammad and the Qur'an by the verse that follows this one, and its interpretation is apparent.

Then He informed that they did not say that on the basis of clear evidence, nor did they deny Muhammad with certainty, and no scripture or prophet had come to them before him informing them of the corruption of his affair. So He said: ﴿And We did not give them any books which they could study﴾. Qatadah said: Allah did not send down to the Arabs a scripture before the Qur'an, nor did He send to them a prophet before Muhammad. This is understood as referring to those whom our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) warned; and Isma'il had been a warner to the Arabs.

Then He informed of the outcome of those who denied before them, as a warning to them, saying:

﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them﴾. Here there are three opinions.

The first: the disbelievers of Makkah did not reach a tenth of what We gave the nations before them of strength, wealth, and long life. This is the view of the majority.

The second: those before them did not reach a tenth of what We gave these [people] of proof and evidence.

The third: those before them did not reach a tenth of the gratitude for what We gave them. Al-Mawardi related these two.

Al-Mi'shar means a tenth. And al-Nakir is a noun meaning denial. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is, "How was My denial?" The yā' was omitted because it is the end of a verse.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 34, verse 51–54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified﴾ — regarding the time of this terror, there are two opinions.

One: that it is at the time of resurrection from the graves. This was said by most of the scholars.

The second: that it is at the appearance of the punishment in this world. It was related by al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Qatadah also said this. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: it is the army that will be swallowed up by the earth in al-Bayda', of whom one man will remain to inform the people of what befell them. This is a hadith explained in the tafsir, that this army will head toward the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram) to destroy it, and they will be swallowed up. Al-Dahhak and Zayd ibn Aslam said: this verse refers to those among the polytheists who were killed on the Day of Badr.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then there will be no escape﴾ — the meaning: there will be no escape for them, i.e., they will not be able to escape from Us. ﴿And they will be seized from a near place﴾ — regarding this there are three opinions.

One: from their place on the Day of Badr; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam. The second: from beneath their feet by being swallowed up; this was said by Muqatil. The third: from the graves; this was said by Ibn Qutaybah. Wherever they were, they are near to Allah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say﴾ — that is, when they witness the punishment — ﴿We have believed in it﴾ — regarding the pronoun in "bihi" (in it) there are four opinions.

One: that it refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; this was said by Mujahid. The second: that it refers to the resurrection; this was said by al-Hasan. The third: that it refers to the Messenger; this was said by Qatadah. The fourth: that it refers to the Qur'an; this was said by Muqatil.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how can they reach [faith] from a distant place?﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Ibn ʿAmir, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "al-tanawush" without hamza. Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim read it with hamza. Al-Farra' said: whoever reads with hamza makes it from "na'ashtu," and whoever does not make it hamzah makes it from "nushtu," and the two are close in meaning; the meaning is: I reached for the thing, in the same way as: dhimtu al-shay' and dha'amtuhu, meaning I found fault with it. The people "tanawashu" in battle when some of them reach others with spears without coming fully close. The hamza of "al-tanā'ush" may also be applied, and it is from "nushtu," because of the connection of the waw, like His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time﴾ [al-Mursalat: 11]. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever makes hamza in "al-tanā'ush" does so because the waw of "al-tanawush" is dammah, and every waw with a dammah whose dammah is fixed may, if you wish, be replaced by a hamza, and if you wish, not be replaced, as in: ādu'ur. Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of the verse: ﴿And how can they reach [it]﴾ — for what they wished to attain and to achieve what they sought of repentance — ﴿from a distant place﴾, which is the place where repentance is accepted. Likewise the exegetes said: how can they reach faith and repentance, when they abandoned that in this world, and the world has passed away?

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they had already disbelieved in it﴾ — regarding the pronoun in "bihi" there are four opinions already mentioned in His saying: ﴿We have believed in it﴾ [Saba': 52]. The meaning of ﴿before﴾ is: in this world, before witnessing the terrors of the Hereafter. ﴿And they would hurl [accusations] about the unseen﴾ — that is, they would throw out conjecture — ﴿from a distant place﴾, which is their distance from knowledge of what they were saying.

Regarding the intended meaning of this statement of theirs there are three opinions.

One: that they think they will be returned to the world; this was said by Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: that it is their saying in this world: there is no resurrection for us, nor Paradise, nor Fire; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that it is their saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he is a sorcerer, he is a soothsayer, he is a poet; this was said by Mujahid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ — that is, these disbelievers will be prevented from what they desire, and regarding this there are six opinions.

One: that it is the return to the world; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. The second: family, wealth, and children; this was said by Mujahid. The third: faith; this was said by al-Hasan. The fourth: obedience to Allah; this was said by Qatadah. The fifth: repentance; this was said by al-Suddi. The sixth: between the army that went out to destroy the Ka'bah and that, by their being swallowed up; this was said by Muqatil.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As was done﴾ — and Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Abu ʿImran read "kama fa'ala" with fatha on the fa' and the ʿayn — ﴿with their sects before﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, with those whose way was their way. The exegetes said: the meaning is: as was done to their counterparts among the disbelievers before these, for they too were prevented from what they desired. Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of the Elephant when they intended to destroy the Ka'bah. ﴿Indeed, they were in doubt﴾ — about the resurrection and the descent of punishment upon them — ﴿disquieting﴾, that is, causing unease and suspicion.

One: from their place on the Day of Badr; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam. The second: from beneath their feet by being swallowed up; this was said by Muqatil. The third: from the graves; this was said by Ibn Qutaybah. Wherever they were, they are near to Allah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say﴾ — that is, when they witness the punishment — ﴿We have believed in it﴾ — regarding the pronoun in "bihi" (in it) there are four opinions.

One: that it refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; this was said by Mujahid. The second: that it refers to the resurrection; this was said by al-Hasan. The third: that it refers to the Messenger; this was said by Qatadah. The fourth: that it refers to the Qur'an; this was said by Muqatil.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how can they reach [faith] from a distant place?﴾ — Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Ibn ʿAmir, and Hafs from ʿAsim read "al-tanawush" without hamza. Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim read it with hamza. Al-Farra' said: whoever reads with hamza makes it from "na'ashtu," and whoever does not make it hamzah makes it from "nushtu," and the two are close in meaning; the meaning is: I reached for the thing, in the same way as: dhimtu al-shay' and dha'amtuhu, meaning I found fault with it. The people "tanawashu" in battle when some of them reach others with spears without coming fully close. The hamza of "al-tanā'ush" may also be applied, and it is from "nushtu," because of the connection of the waw, like His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered at their appointed time﴾ [al-Mursalat: 11]. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever makes hamza in "al-tanā'ush" does so because the waw of "al-tanawush" is dammah, and every waw with a dammah whose dammah is fixed may, if you wish, be replaced by a hamza, and if you wish, not be replaced, as in: ādu'ur. Ibn Qutaybah said: the meaning of the verse: ﴿And how can they reach [it]﴾ — for what they wished to attain and to achieve what they sought of repentance — ﴿from a distant place﴾, which is the place where repentance is accepted. Likewise the exegetes said: how can they reach faith and repentance, when they abandoned that in this world, and the world has passed away?

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they had already disbelieved in it﴾ — regarding the pronoun in "bihi" there are four opinions already mentioned in His saying: ﴿We have believed in it﴾ [Saba': 52]. The meaning of ﴿before﴾ is: in this world, before witnessing the terrors of the Hereafter. ﴿And they would hurl [accusations] about the unseen﴾ — that is, they would throw out conjecture — ﴿from a distant place﴾, which is their distance from knowledge of what they were saying.

Regarding the intended meaning of this statement of theirs there are three opinions.

One: that they think they will be returned to the world; this was said by Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: that it is their saying in this world: there is no resurrection for us, nor Paradise, nor Fire; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that it is their saying about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he is a sorcerer, he is a soothsayer, he is a poet; this was said by Mujahid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ — that is, these disbelievers will be prevented from what they desire, and regarding this there are six opinions.

One: that it is the return to the world; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. The second: family, wealth, and children; this was said by Mujahid. The third: faith; this was said by al-Hasan. The fourth: obedience to Allah; this was said by Qatadah. The fifth: repentance; this was said by al-Suddi. The sixth: between the army that went out to destroy the Ka'bah and that, by their being swallowed up; this was said by Muqatil.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As was done﴾ — and Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Abu ʿImran read "kama fa'ala" with fatha on the fa' and the ʿayn — ﴿with their sects before﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, with those whose way was their way. The exegetes said: the meaning is: as was done to their counterparts among the disbelievers before these, for they too were prevented from what they desired. Al-Dahhak said: they are the companions of the Elephant when they intended to destroy the Ka'bah. ﴿Indeed, they were in doubt﴾ — about the resurrection and the descent of punishment upon them — ﴿disquieting﴾, that is, causing unease and suspicion.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 34, verse 51–54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified﴾ — regarding the time of this terror, there are two opinions.

One: that it is at the time of resurrection from the graves. This was said by most of the scholars.

The second: that it is at the appearance of the punishment in this world. It was related by al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Qatadah also said this.
